terms.gloss: a little ball blown up with air: a balloon
evidence: Suet. Aug. 83: ad pilam folliculumque trānsiit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a small bag, and so “a ball to play with, inflated with air” (Lewis & Short), the game Augustus took up after the civil wars (Suet. Aug. 83). Its use for a toy balloon is modern: Levi and Bini give it for the Italian palloncino (p. 45). Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for a balloon.

terms.gloss: bladder; extended here to an inflated balloon
terms.comment: Our extension of the word for a bladder, which is used classically of things made of one, a purse, a lantern, or a football (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: a ball blown up with air

sources: Lewis & Short: vesica · Lewis & Short: follis
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 45, s.v. palloncino.
